paradoxes.text: The EU pays Mauritania to stop people heading north, yet the 150,000-person inflow it hosts comes from Mali, a flow the payment does not reach: the leverage is spent on the Atlantic route while the pressure arrives on the eastern border.

grand_strategy.reading: Mauritania is paid to be a border: Europe buys its enforcement against migrants heading north, while the Malian crisis puts about 150,000 refugees on its eastern side. Its UN votes follow a conventional line, with yes on the 2022 Ukraine aggression resolution and abstention on the 2025 peace text. The card is thin: the 2024 Mali border incidents, the Morocco and Algeria dossiers and the China, US, Russia and Gulf positions remain open gaps.

stances.note: Transactional: the EU pays (EUR 210m, 2024) for Mauritania's control of migration toward Europe, with no alignment. Warming rests on that 2024 money deal alone; no later source was checked. Bond none: pure interest, nothing underneath.
